evaluations.query: run multiple npm scripts in parallel or sequence with one command, like concurrently or npm-run-all
evaluations.reason: All three place GT npm-run-all at #1 and recommend very similar alternatives. Method B edges ahead with @xarc/run which adds diversity beyond forks. A and C both include yarn-run-all and npm-run-all2 which are essentially forks of the same tool.

evaluations.query: generate HTML coverage report from LCOV data, grouped by directory and file
evaluations.reason: All three have GT @lcov-viewer/cli at #1. Method A adds lcoview as a distinct alternative at #2, offering more diversity. Method B is also solid. Method C has a duplicate entry for @lcov-viewer/cli at #1 and #2, reducing its value.

evaluations.query: NestJS authentication module with JWT, user registration and login out of the box
evaluations.reason: None recommend the GT. Method C at least mentions NestJS-related tools (@rucken/cli, nicot with NestJS). Method B has login-express and generic auth middleware — somewhat relevant but not NestJS-specific. Method A recommends a Gatsby docs theme at #1 which is completely off-topic.

evaluations.query: remap code coverage results from compiled JS back to original source using source maps
evaluations.reason: Method B places GT remap-istanbul at #1, plus istanbul-sourcemap-report and map-coverage — all directly relevant. Method A has istanbul-sourcemap-report at #1 which is relevant but misses GT. Method C is similar to A but with different ordering.

evaluations.query: JavaScript implementation of IEEE 754 copysign function, copy sign from one float to another
evaluations.reason: Methods A and C both have GT at #1 and math-float64-copysign at #2, both excellent. A's #3 math-float64-to-words is related to float internals. C's #3 numeric is a general numerical library. Method B recommends maprange and CSS converters — completely irrelevant to copysign.

evaluations.query: TypeScript SDK for robotics device control and service management
evaluations.reason: All three have GT at #1 and @cognite/robotics-ts-sdk at #2. Method C's #3 rclnodejs (ROS2 JS client) is highly relevant for robotics. Method A's #3 robotics-dev is also relevant. Method B's #3 imt-mcp-server is about device control but less robotics-focused.
